extracted.intended_audience: U.S. Senate Committee on Energy and Natural Resources; Reclamation leadership, staff, water and power customers, and other stakeholders
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for implementing the NRC's recommendations and the Bureau of Reclamation's "Managing for Excellence" action plan, including organization, staffing, stakeholder engagement, scheduling, funding, and reporting expectations. Focused on improving Reclamation's capability to manage construction, infrastructure, operations, and stakeholder relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nine issue areas for NRC recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: The NRC focused its recommendations for Reclamation in nine issue areas: centralized policy and decentralized operations; Reclamation’s technical service center; Laboratory and research activities; Outsourcing; Asset sustainment planning; Project management; Acquisition and contracting; Relationships with sponsors and stakeholders; and Workforce and human resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these nine areas as the organizing framework for review and implementation; each area contains findings and recommendations to be addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralized policy and decentralized operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies, procedures, and standards should be developed centrally and implemented locally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance the need for consistency in Reclamation policies and decisions with local operational autonomy; central development + local implementation is the prescribed model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical Services Center (TSC) assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Reclamation should perform an in-depth review of its own Technical Services Center to identify the core competencies it needs, the number of personnel it needs, and its optimum structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The TSC assessment should be reviewed by independent experts and stakeholders; use the review to right-size and reconfigure TSC functions and staffing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laboratory and research right-sizing
rubrics_metrics.description: Reclamation’s laboratory organization and its physical structures may be too large.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate laboratory organization and facilities for excess scale and reorganize or downsize where appropriate to improve efficiency and fit mission needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outsourcing of O&M and other functions
rubrics_metrics.description: O&M and other functions should be more aggressively outsourced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider outsourcing where it makes good business sense to improve efficiency and focus internal resources on core mission activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asset sustainment planning and innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Long-term sustainment of aging infrastructure will require more innovation and greater efficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize long-term sustainment strategies that emphasize innovative approaches and improved efficiency to preserve infrastructure value over decades.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project management and cost estimating discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Reclamation should give high priority to completing and publishing cost estimating directives and resist efforts to submit projects to Congress with incomplete project planning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish authoritative cost estimating directives and ensure projects are presented only when planning and estimates are complete and defensible; restore confidence in project cost-estimating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acquisition and contracting improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: Acquisition and contracting are identified as an issue area requiring attention and improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review and reform acquisition and contracting practices to support efficient, transparent procurement consistent with action-plan goals (specific practices to be developed in action items).

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationships with sponsors and stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: Reclamation’s customers and other stakeholders want close contact with empowered Reclamation officials, but they also want consistency in Reclamation policies and decisions, and decision makers with demonstrated professional competence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foster close, empowered contact while maintaining consistency; engage a broad spectrum of stakeholders in decisions, potentially sharing or transferring O&M management and decision-making to customers where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workforce and human resources development
rubrics_metrics.description: The growing need to include a broad spectrum of stakeholders alters Reclamation’s tasks and the skills required to accomplish them. Personnel must be equipped to address both technical uncertainties and the ambiguities of future social and environmental outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in training, staffing, and organizational changes that equip employees to handle technical and social/environmental complexity; solicit rank-and-file input in implementing changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of independent experts and stakeholder review
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessments (e.g., of the TSC) should be reviewed by independent experts and stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate outside expert review and stakeholder perspectives into internal assessments to improve credibility and robustness of decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action items must have clear schedules
rubrics_metrics.description: Managing for Excellence is a catalogue of 41 separate action items; each action item has a specific start date and end date. The timetable is ambitious; all but twelve of the 41 action items are scheduled to be completed (i.e., recommendations forwarded to Reclamation senior management) in 2006.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set start/end dates and enforce schedules so decisions are made in a timely but adequate period; timelines should be sufficient 'to get it right' without unduly delaying benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action-team composition and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Action teams are made up of individuals known for intellectual honesty and for being committed to carrying out the Reclamation mission; they have established a reputation for ingenuity and achievement in communication, consultation, and cooperation with diverse stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select teams for integrity, commitment, and stakeholder engagement skills; each team should prepare a work plan including timelines from data gathering through analysis to final decision recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work plans and explicit deliverables
rubrics_metrics.description: Each action team has prepared a work plan which includes timelines for steps from gathering data and perspectives, to analysis, to final decision recommendations on the schedule set out in Managing for Excellence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require explicit work plans and deliverables for each action item; include roles, milestones, and decision points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder involvement requirement for credibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Roughly half of the action items cannot be credibly addressed without direct input from water and power customers; other items depend on wisdom of rank-and-file employees, changes to legislation, or expert guidance from government management experts inside and outside the Department of the Interior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify which action items require external stakeholder input or legislative/expert action and secure that input as part of the workplan before final decisions are made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding via reprioritization with mission protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding to carry out the tasks contemplated in the plan will be made available by reprioritizing existing activities. Reclamation’s reprioritization of funds will be carried out consistent with an absolute commitment to ensure that all activities vital to Reclamation’s core mission, including ongoing operation, maintenance, and environmental compliance responsibilities, are unaffected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reallocate resources internally but protect core mission activities; document funding decisions and tradeoffs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expected outcomes: efficiency and capacity improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: Implementation of the action items will result in significant improvements in the efficiency of Reclamation’s management. This would ultimately translate into improved capacity to carry out all aspects of Reclamation’s mission, including operation, maintenance, and environmental compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure implementation success by gains in management efficiency and mission capacity (e.g., O&M performance, environmental compliance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and reporting of action items
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit for the record a chart describing each of the 41 action items with each item’s start and end date and team leader, as well as a chart that depicts the integrated schedule for all action items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide public/legislative reporting of action-item schedules, leaders, and integrated timelines to enable oversight and accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balanced scheduling principle
rubrics_metrics.description: The schedule was carefully considered to make certain that each decision was afforded enough time to get it right but not so much time that the benefits of implementing decisions would be needlessly delayed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt scheduling that balances thoroughness and timeliness; avoid open-ended decision timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow PART-directed strategic planning
rubrics_metrics.description: The PART directed the Bureau to, '[D]evelop a comprehensive, long-term strategy to operate, maintain, and rehabilitate Reclamation facilities'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the action plan dovetails with PART assessments and includes a comprehensive long-term strategy for facility operation, maintenance, and rehabilitation.
